# CloverDX Lookup Tables — LLM Generation Reference

> Graph-level asset declared in `<Global>`, not a component. Components reference it via `lookupTable="<id>"`.

---

## LOOKUP TABLE TYPES

| Type | In Memory | Key Duplicates | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`simpleLookup`** | Yes (all data) | Yes | Default. Point-lookup enrichment, dimension key resolution. Fits in JVM heap. |
| **`dbLookup`** | No (LRU cache optional) | Yes | Reference data lives in a DB; too large or too dynamic for memory. |
| **`rangeLookup`** | Yes (all data) | No (overlapping intervals OK) | Key is a range (start/end fields). Rate tables, tax brackets, date-effective mappings. |
| **`persistentLookup`** | No (B+Tree files, small cache) | Configurable | Very large reference data that won't fit in memory; B+Tree on disk. |
| **`aspellLookup`** | Yes | Yes | Fuzzy / approximate string matching (address correction, spell-checking). |
| **Reference lookup** | Yes | No | Server Reference Data Set — approved/published reference rows only. Server projects only. |

**Default choice:** `simpleLookup` covers the vast majority of cases. Only deviate when the data is too large for memory (`persistentLookup`, `dbLookup`) or requires range semantics (`rangeLookup`).

> **Warning:** Do not use lookup tables in `init()`, `preExecute()`, or `postExecute()` CTL functions.

---

## SKELETONS

### simpleLookup — populated at runtime (dominant pattern)

```xml
<!-- In <Global> -->
<LookupTable id="LT_COUNTRIES" type="simpleLookup"
             metadata="META_COUNTRIES"
             key="country_code"
             initialSize="1000"/>
```

Populated in phase 0 via `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER`, consumed in phase 1 via `LOOKUP_JOIN` or CTL `lookup()`.

### simpleLookup — populated from file at phase start

```xml
<LookupTable id="LT_PRODUCTS" type="simpleLookup"
             metadata="META_PRODUCTS"
             key="product_id"
             initialSize="5000"
             fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/products.csv"/>
```

Engine loads the CSV once at phase start. No `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` needed. File must exist before the phase runs.

### dbLookup

```xml
<LookupTable id="LT_CUSTOMERS" type="dbLookup"
             metadata="META_CUSTOMERS"
             dbConnection="JDBC0"
             sqlQuery="SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id = ?"
             maxCached="1000"
             storeNulls="false"/>
```

### aspellLookup

```xml
<LookupTable dataFileCharset="UTF-8" dataFileUrl="${LOOKUP_DIR}/streets.dat" editDistanceField="ed" id="LookupTable0" lookupKeyField="name" metadata="Metadata0" name="streets" type="aspellLookup"/>
```

Critical Aspell key rule:
- Use `lookupKeyField="..."` on the `<LookupTable>` element.

### rangeLookup

```xml
<LookupTable id="LT_TAX" type="rangeLookup"
             metadata="META_TAX_BRACKETS"
             startFields="income_from"
             endFields="income_to"
             startInclude="true"
             endInclude="true"/>
```

- `startFields` / `endFields` name the metadata fields that hold the interval boundaries.
- `startInclude` / `endInclude` are **booleans** (`true`/`false`) — whether the boundary is included in the interval. Defaults: `startInclude=true`, `endInclude=false`, giving a `[start, end)` interval. Set both to `true` for `[start, end]` (inclusive on both sides), which is usually correct for date ranges.
- There is **no `key` attribute** on `rangeLookup`. The probe value is passed to `.get(probeValue)` directly; the engine finds the row whose `[startField, endField]` interval contains the probe value.

### simpleLookup — inline data (small static sets)

Data embedded directly in the graph XML as a CDATA block. No external file, no pre-load phase. Use for small, rarely-changing reference data (country codes, department names, status mappings, etc.).

```xml
<!-- Metadata defines field names, types, and delimiter used to parse the inline rows -->
<Metadata id="DeptLookupMetadata">
    <Record name="Department" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter="|">
        <Field name="code" type="string"/>
        <Field name="dept_name" type="string"/>
    </Record>
</Metadata>

<LookupTable id="DeptInlineLookup" type="simpleLookup"
             metadata="DeptLookupMetadata" key="code">
    <Data><![CDATA[HR|Human Resources
IT|Information Technology
FIN|Finance and Accounting
MKT|Marketing and Sales]]></Data>
</LookupTable>
```

Key points:
- `fieldDelimiter` on the `<Record>` controls how each row is parsed — must match the data format in `<Data>`.
- No `fileURL`, no `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` needed — the engine loads the CDATA at phase start.
- The CTL type name for `lookup().get()` is the `<Record name="...">` value (`Department` here).
- Keep data small — large inline blocks bloat the graph XML and make diffs unreadable. For more than a few hundred rows, use `fileURL` or `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` instead.

### persistentLookup

```xml
<LookupTable id="LT_BIG" type="persistentLookup"
             metadata="META_BIG"
             key="record_id"
             fileURL="${LOOKUP_DIR}/big_lookup"
             keyDuplicates="false"/>
```

Two files are created: `big_lookup.db` and `big_lookup.lg`.

---

## `<LookupTable>` XML ATTRIBUTES

| Attribute | Types | Req | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | all | yes | Unique within graph. Referenced by `lookupTable=` on components and by `lookup(name)` in CTL (uses `name=`, see below). |
| `type` | all | yes | `simpleLookup`, `dbLookup`, `rangeLookup`, `persistentLookup`, `aspellLookup`. |
| `metadata` | all | yes | ID of a `<Metadata>` element. Defines record structure and CSV parsing (fieldDelimiter etc.) for file-backed lookups. |
| `name` | all | yes | Human label — also the identifier used in CTL2 `lookup(name)` calls. |
| `key` | simple/persistent | yes | Semicolon-separated field name(s) from the metadata that form the lookup key. **Not used by `rangeLookup`** — use `startFields`/`endFields` instead. |
| `startFields` | rangeLookup | yes | Semicolon-separated field name(s) for the interval start boundary (e.g. `"valid_from"`). |
| `endFields` | rangeLookup | yes | Semicolon-separated field name(s) for the interval end boundary (e.g. `"valid_to"`). |
| `startInclude` | rangeLookup | no | Semicolon-separated booleans — whether the start boundary is included (`true`=≥, `false`=>). Default `true`. |
| `endInclude` | rangeLookup | no | Semicolon-separated booleans — whether the end boundary is included (`true`=≤, `false`=<). Default `false`. Set to `true` for fully-closed `[start, end]` date ranges. |
| `initialSize` | simpleLookup | no | HashMap initial capacity hint (default 512). Set to approximate row count to avoid rehashing. |
| `fileURL` | simple/range/persistent | no | Path to data file loaded at phase start. Supports `${PARAM}` substitution. |
| `charset` | simple/range | no | Encoding for file-loaded data (default UTF-8). |
| `keyDuplicates` | simple/persistent | no | `true` = multiple records per key; `false` = last (or first, with `replace=false`) wins. |
| `dbConnection` | dbLookup | yes | ID of a `<Connection>` in `<Global>`. |
| `sqlQuery` | dbLookup | yes | SQL with `WHERE field = ?` placeholder(s) — one `?` per key field. |
| `maxCached` | dbLookup | no | LRU cache size (number of records). 0 = no cache. |
| `storeNulls` | dbLookup | no | `true` = cache "not found" responses to avoid repeated DB hits. |
| `freeLookupTable` | — | no | On `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` / `LOOKUP_JOIN`: when `true`, frees memory after the component finishes. |

---

## DATA SOURCES

Three ways to populate a lookup table:

| Method | How | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **`fileURL` on `<LookupTable>`** | Engine reads the file at phase start | Static reference data already in a file; no pre-load phase needed |
| **`LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER`** (phase 0) | Component writes input records into the table | Data sourced from DB, transformation, or another graph output |
| **Inline `<Data>`** | CDATA block embedded directly in `<LookupTable>` in the graph XML | Small, static reference data (e.g. country codes, department names) — no external file or pre-load phase needed |

**Preferred:** `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` for runtime data; `fileURL` for static seed files.

---

## TWO-PHASE POPULATION PATTERN

The lookup table must be fully populated **before** any consumer reads from it. The standard pattern:

```xml
<Global>
  <LookupTable id="LT_COUNTRIES" type="simpleLookup"
               metadata="META_COUNTRIES" key="country_code" initialSize="300"/>
</Global>

<!-- Phase 0: populate -->
<Node id="READ_REF" type="FLAT_FILE_READER"
      fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/countries.csv" guiX="100" guiY="50" phase="0"/>
<Node id="LOAD_LT" type="LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER"
      lookupTable="LT_COUNTRIES" guiX="400" guiY="50" phase="0"/>
<Edge fromNode="READ_REF:0" toNode="LOAD_LT:0"/>

<!-- Phase 1: consume -->
<Node id="JOIN0" type="LOOKUP_JOIN"
      lookupTable="LT_COUNTRIES" joinKey="country_code" leftOuterJoin="true"
      guiX="400" guiY="250" phase="1">
  <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.* = $in.0.*;
    $out.0.country_name = isnull($in.1.name) ? "UNKNOWN" : $in.1.name;
    return ALL;
}
  ]]></attr>
</Node>
```

---

## CTL2 USAGE

### Direct lookup in REFORMAT / FILTER etc.

```ctl
//#CTL2
// Typed record variable — type name is the <Record name="..."> from the metadata
META_COUNTRIES country = lookup(LT_COUNTRIES).get($in.0.country_code);

$out.0.country_name = isnull(country) ? "UNKNOWN" : country.name;
```

- `lookup(name)` — `name` is the `name=` attribute on `<LookupTable>`, not the `id`.
- `.get(key)` returns null when the key is not found — always guard with `isnull()`.
- `.get(key)` with composite key: `lookup(LT).get(field1, field2)`.
- `.next()` — iterate over duplicate-key matches (simpleLookup with `allowKeyDuplicates="true"`).

### In LOOKUP_JOIN transform

The lookup record appears as `$in.1` — there is **no slave input port**:

```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.*             = $in.0.*;
    $out.0.country_name  = isnull($in.1.name) ? "UNKNOWN" : $in.1.name;
    return ALL;
}
```

---

## EXTERNAL (SHARED) LOOKUP TABLES

A lookup table can be stored in an external `.lkp` file and linked into multiple graphs — same concept as `.fmt` for metadata or `.cfg` for connections.

**Graph reference — the XML attribute is `lookupConfig`, NOT `fileURL`:**
```xml
<LookupTable id="LookupTable0" lookupConfig="${LOOKUP_DIR}/dbLookup0.lkp"/>
```

- The `<LookupTable lookupConfig="...">` element carries **only `id` and `lookupConfig`** — no `type`, `metadata`, `key`, or `dbConnection` attributes. Those live inside the `.lkp` file itself.
- Stored under `lookup/` directory in the sandbox. File extension is conventionally `.lkp` (some older examples use `.cfg`).
- Shared across graphs — change the file, all linked graphs pick it up.
---

### `.lkp` FILE FORMAT

A `.lkp` file is **Java Properties format** — key=value lines, one property per line, colons and `$` backslash-escaped. **Not XML.**

**dbLookup example (`lookup/dbLookup0.lkp`):**
```
#Fri Jun 12 20:52:06 CEST 2026
dbConnection=${CONN_DIR}/notesdb.cfg
maxCached=0
metadata=${META_DIR}/album.fmt
name=dbLookup0
sqlQuery=select * from album where names\=$1
storeNulls=true
type=dbLookup
```

**simpleLookup example (`lookup/LT_Countries.lkp`):**
```
#Thu Jun 12 12:00:00 CEST 2026
initialSize=300
key=country_code
metadata=${META_DIR}/countries.fmt
name=LT_COUNTRIES
type=simpleLookup
```

**persistentLookup example:**
```
#Thu Jun 12 12:00:00 CEST 2026
keyDuplicates=false
fileURL=${LOOKUP_DIR}/big_lookup
key=record_id
metadata=${META_DIR}/big.fmt
name=LT_BIG
type=persistentLookup
```

**Escaping rules** (same as `.cfg`):

| Char | In `.lkp` |
|---|---|
| `:` | `\:` |
| `$` | `\$` (inside values like SQL — `names\=$1`) |
| `=` | `\=` |
| `\` | `\\` |

---

### DEPENDENCY LINKING (LLM obligation)

When Designer links a `.lkp`, it reads the file, discovers `metadata=` and `dbConnection=` properties, and automatically adds corresponding `<Metadata>` and `<Connection>` elements to `<Global>`. **The LLM must do this manually.**

**Key structural rules:**
- The `<LookupTable lookupConfig="...">` element has ONLY `id` and `lookupConfig` — it does NOT get `metadata=` or `dbConnection=` attributes. The engine reads those from the `.lkp` file itself at runtime.
- The `<Metadata>` and `<Connection>` elements are added as **independent** external references in `<Global>`. They are not cross-referenced by ID from the `<LookupTable>` element — they simply need to be declared so that the Designer and runtime engine can validate and resolve them.

| `.lkp` property | What to add to `<Global>` |
|---|---|
| `metadata=<path>` | `<Metadata fileURL="<path>" id="<id>"/>` — if not already present |
| `dbConnection=<path>` | `<Connection dbConfig="<path>" id="<id>" type="JDBC"/>` — if not already present |

**Example** — linking `dbLookup0.lkp` (which has `metadata=${META_DIR}/album.fmt` and `dbConnection=${CONN_DIR}/notesdb.cfg`) requires adding **three** independent entries to `<Global>`:

```xml
<!-- 1. The lookup — only id + lookupConfig; no type/metadata/dbConnection here -->
<LookupTable id="LookupTable0" lookupConfig="${LOOKUP_DIR}/dbLookup0.lkp"/>

<!-- 2. Metadata — standalone external reference; NOT linked by id from the LookupTable element -->
<Metadata id="Metadata0" fileURL="${META_DIR}/album.fmt"/>

<!-- 3. Connection — standalone external reference; NOT linked by id from the LookupTable element -->
<Connection id="JDBC0" dbConfig="${CONN_DIR}/notesdb.cfg" type="JDBC"/>
```

Choose `id` values that are unique within the graph. If a `<Metadata>` or `<Connection>` with the same `fileURL` / `dbConfig` is already present in `<Global>`, reuse it — do not add a duplicate.

---

## GENERATION RULES

- `<LookupTable>` must be in `<Global>`, not inside a `<Phase>`.
- `id` must be unique in the graph. Components reference it via `lookupTable="<id>"`.
- `name` is the CTL2 handle used in `lookup(name)` — keep it descriptive and unique.
- `key` must match field name(s) from the referenced `metadata`.
- Population (LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER or fileURL) must happen **before** any consumer phase.
- `simpleLookup` is the default choice. Only use `dbLookup` / `persistentLookup` when data is too large for memory.
- `fileURL` on `<LookupTable>` is for loading data INTO the lookup at phase start — it is **not** an external file reference for sharing the lookup definition. For sharing the definition across graphs, use `.lkp` externalized files.
- When writing a new `.lkp` file: use Java Properties format (key=value, one per line, colons and `$` backslash-escaped) — **not XML**.
- When linking an external `.lkp` into a graph: read the file and also add `<Metadata>` and `<Connection>` entries to `<Global>` for every `metadata=` and `dbConnection=` reference found in the `.lkp`. Designer does this automatically; the LLM must do it explicitly.
- Inline `<Data>` CDATA is a valid production pattern for small static sets (codes, mappings). The `fieldDelimiter` on `<Record>` must match the data format. For more than ~a few hundred rows, use `fileURL` or `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` to keep graph XML readable.
- `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` has no CTL transform — never add a `transform` attribute to it.
- Always use `leftOuterJoin="true"` on `LOOKUP_JOIN` unless you explicitly want unmatched records dropped; unmatched records silently go to port 1 and are discarded if port 1 is unconnected.
- Do not use lookup tables in `init()`, `preExecute()`, or `postExecute()` CTL functions.

---

## COMMON MISTAKES

| Mistake | Fix |
|---|---|
| `<LookupTable>` inside `<Phase>` | Must be in `<Global>`. |
| Lookup populated in the same phase as the consumer | Populate in phase N, consume in phase N+1 or later. |
| `joinKey` uses `#` or `(a)/(d)` suffix | LOOKUP_JOIN `joinKey` is plain driver field names, semicolon-separated. `#` is EXT_HASH_JOIN syntax; `(a)/(d)` is EXT_MERGE_JOIN — both cause `Join key parsing error` here. |
| `lookup(id)` in CTL — using `id` instead of `name` | CTL `lookup()` takes the `name=` attribute, not the `id=`. |
| Whole-record null check `isnull($in.1)` with leftOuterJoin | Test a concrete field: `isnull($in.1.some_field)`. Whole-record null check does not work. |
| Missing `leftOuterJoin="true"` — unmatched records silently dropped | Default is `false` — unmatched go to port 1; if unconnected they are discarded. Use `leftOuterJoin="true"` for keep-all semantics. |
| `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` with a `transform` attribute | This component has no CTL transform. Remove the attribute. |
| Writing to a `dbLookup` via `LOOKUP_TABLE_READER_WRITER` | Not supported. `dbLookup` is read-only from the graph side. |
| `initialSize` too small — silent rehashing | Set `initialSize` to approximate row count. Does not cap the table, only affects initial allocation. |
| Large simpleLookup exhausting heap | Use `dbLookup` (with cache) or `persistentLookup` for data that doesn't fit in JVM heap. |
| `fileURL` on `<LookupTable>` — file not present at phase start | The phase fails immediately. Ensure the file exists before the phase runs (produced by an earlier phase or a seed file). |
| Confusing `fileURL` (data source) with `lookupConfig` (external definition) | `fileURL` loads data rows into the lookup at phase start. `lookupConfig` points to an external `.lkp` definition file — use this when linking a shared lookup definition. These are separate attributes with completely different purposes. |
| `.lkp` file written as XML | `.lkp` is Java Properties format — key=value, one per line, `$` and `:` backslash-escaped. XML belongs only in the graph file's `<LookupTable>` element. |
| Linking a `.lkp` without adding its dependencies | After adding `<LookupTable id="..." lookupConfig="...lkp"/>`, read the file and add `<Metadata>` for every `metadata=` and `<Connection>` for every `dbConnection=` found. These are standalone entries in `<Global>` — they are NOT cross-referenced from the `<LookupTable>` element. Missing declarations cause a "not found" error at graph load time. |
